clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Mining is an introductory quest that teaches miners how to craft a lodestone to enhance wilderness campsites. Instructed by Gelman Stonehand in Stormwind, prospectors learn to channel resonant earthcraft to bolster their companions' combat prowess around the campfire.

Mining is tough, honest labor, but its rewards go far beyond smelting raw ingots and shaping armor. Dedicated miners in Stormwind can learn to harness the natural magnetism of the earth into a functional lodestone. When placed at an expedition's campsite, this stone bolsters the combat vigor of any fighter gathered around the hearth fire. Gelman Stonehand, the seasoned mining instructor in the kingdom's capital, passes down the craft to prospectors who demonstrate proficiency with a pickaxe.

A lodestone cannot simply be dropped onto the cobblestones of Cathedral Square or the Trade District. Townsfolk take a dim view of travelers pitching temporary encampments within city limits, meaning pioneers must head out into the untamed wilds to establish camp. Furthermore, specialized gear like a lodestone is useless without the warm foundation of a campfire, a fundamental wilderness survival skill taught by cooks across the realm.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Mining isn't the most glamorous, but it's good honest work and a fine profession for you to explore.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Lodestone for your camp. Build one of these and everyone who wants to swing a sword will be eager to gather round your fire and soak up the extra "oomph" it can provide to increase their combat prowess.

clips.title: Progress
paras: I can show you some things, if you have the aptitude.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Lodestone. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
